title: Microfluidic Bioprinting for Engineering Vascularized Tissues and Organoids
protocol: Insert a smaller blunt needle into the center of a larger blunt needle to construct the dual-layer, concentric microfluidic printhead.
Adjust the alignment so that the core needle protrudes slightly (~1 mm) longer than the outer shell.
Seal the junction of the barrels with epoxy glue and remove any alignment spacers from the tip side if necessary.
Insert another needle in the barrel of the central needle in the reverse direction.
Generate a hole on the side of the barrel of the outer needle and insert a metal connector into the hole.
Seal the connection between the needle and the metal connector with epoxy glue.
Connect the inlets of the printhead to a dual-channel syringe pump through two PVC tubes.
Mount the extruder onto the head of a bioprinter using a plastic holder made of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA).
Dissociate human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) from the flasks using treatment by 0.05 w/v% trypsin for 5 - 10 min.
Resuspend HUVECs in bioink at a concentration of 5 - 10 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Pipette cell suspension slowly 5 to 10 times to ensure homogenous distribution.
Start the injection of the bioink/crosslinking fluid using a dual-channel syringe pump.
Allow the flows to stabilize for up to 1 min.
Initiate the movement of the printhead at a deposition speed of approximately 4 mm/s.
Fine tune the speeds with each new setup as needed.
Conduct the bioprinting process at room temperature (21 - 25 °C).
Allow for fast ionic gelation of the alginate component during bioprinting.
Depose a microfibrous scaffold.
Achieve chemical gelation by photocrosslinking the GelMA component with approximately 5 - 10 mW/cm² UV light at 360 - 480 nm for 20 - 30 s.
Gently rinse the scaffold with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to remove excess CaCl₂.
Culture the HUVECs-laden microfibrous scaffold in endothelial cell growth medium (EGM) in an incubator at 37 °C and 5 vol.% CO₂ for up to 16 days.
Change the medium at least every 2 days during culture.
Monitor the morphologies of the HUVECs under a microscope during the culture period.
Retrieve the scaffold once HUVECs have migrated to form lumen-like structures.
Place the scaffold gently on a hydrophobic surface such as polymethylsiloxane (PDMS).
Remove medium from the interstitial space of the scaffold using sterile filter paper with capillary force.
Add a drop (20 - 40 µL) of secondary cell type suspension in medium at density 1 - 10 × 10^6 cells/mL onto the scaffold.
Incubate the configuration in an incubator at 37 °C, 5 vol.% CO2, and 95% relative humidity for 0.5 - 2 h.
Monitor droplet size during incubation to ensure no noticeable evaporation occurs.
Gently wash scaffolds by shaking in a PBS bath to remove non-adherent cells.
Culture the construct in relevant medium until vascularized tissue is formed.
